name: Wavelet and Pyramid Transforms
text:
# Wavelet and Pyramid Transforms

Also called: Transform-based Volume Compression

## Overview
This family encompasses methods that compress volumetric data by decomposing the input volume $V$ into a set of coefficients $C$ using linear transforms (wavelets, pyramids, shearlets), followed by encoding and optional decoding for rendering. It differs from [Value compression](6-value-compression.md) by operating in a transformed frequency domain rather than directly on voxel values, and from [Blockwise Wavelet Compression](6100-blockwise-wavelet-compression.md) by focusing on the global transform structure and its variants rather than the specific block-partitioning optimization.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family share the mechanism of decomposing the input volume $V$ into a set of coefficients $C$ using a linear transform, followed by encoding and optional decoding for rendering.

1. **Transform:** The volume is decomposed using a separable 1D filter bank applied along each axis. For a 3D volume, this results in subbands representing different frequency components. In wavelet transforms, these are typically approximation (low-pass) and detail (high-pass) coefficients. In Laplacian pyramids, they are detail residuals between levels of a [Gaussian pyramid](#7342-hierarchical-3d-gaussian-representations.md) [see [Wavelet and Pyramid Transforms](3856-wavelet-and-pyramid-transforms.md)].
2. **Hierarchy:** The [decomposition](#7254-decomposition.md) is recursive. The approximation subband from level $j$ is further decomposed at level $j+1$, creating a tree-like structure of coefficients. This allows for multi-resolution access, where coarse data is available at the root and fine details are deeper in the tree [see [Value compression](6-value-compression.md)].
3. **[Quantization](#5935-quantization.md) and [Entropy Encoding](#5360-entropy-encoding.md):** Coefficients are quantized (lossy) or kept precise (lossless). Entropy coding (e.g., Huffman, Arithmetic, Run-Length) is applied to the quantized or raw coefficients to produce the compressed bitstream [see [Value compression](6-value-compression.md)].
4. **Reconstruction:** To render, the necessary coefficients are decoded and the inverse transform is applied. This can be done globally (full reconstruction) or locally (block-wise or point-wise) to support adaptive resolution rendering [see [Value compression](6-value-compression.md)].

## Subtopics

### [Laplacian Pyramid Volume Rendering](2261-laplacian-pyramid-volume-rendering.md)
A [direct volume rendering](#1184-direct-volume-rendering.md) technique that reconstructs voxel values on-the-fly from [Laplacian pyramid](#2250-laplacian-pyramid.md) compressed data, utilizing a cache to minimize redundant reconstruction overhead. It forms a [multiresolution representation](#7-multiresolution-and-level-of-detail.md) by pre-applying a Gaussian filter, expansion, and prediction of values, sharing many similarities with wavelet transforms while being optimized for on-the-fly decoding during [ray casting](#6080-ray-casting.md). Choose this when real-time rendering of compressed data is required and cache coherence can be exploited.

### [L2 Norm Wavelet Compression](3542-l2-norm-wavelet-compression.md)
Selects a subset of wavelet coefficients to minimize the $L_2$ error norm of the reconstructed signal relative to the original. It solves the problem of achieving a specific fidelity guarantee while maximizing [compression](#4-compression.md) ratio by discarding the smallest magnitude coefficients. It differs from its siblings, such as [Laplacian Pyramid Volume Rendering](2261-laplacian-pyramid-volume-rendering.md) and [Biorthogonal Wavelet Compression](5381-biorthogonal-wavelet-compression.md), by explicitly sorting coefficients by magnitude to enforce a strict global error bound, rather than relying on perceptual models or fixed bit-depth quantization.

### [B-spline Wavelet Compression](5377-b-spline-wavelet-compression.md)
Decomposes volumetric data into a [multi-resolution hierarchy](#9047-continuous-progressive-levels-of-detail.md) of scaling and wavelet coefficients using B-spline basis functions. It solves the problem of efficiently representing smooth volumetric data by exploiting the linear complexity of the B-spline transform, avoiding the over- and undershoots associated with standard subdivision wavelets. Unlike [L2 Norm Wavelet Compression](3542-l2-norm-wavelet-compression.md) which focuses on error metrics, or [Biorthogonal Wavelet Compression](5381-biorthogonal-wavelet-compression.md) which uses separate primal/dual filters, this method relies on the semi-orthogonality of B-splines, projecting data into dual space for decomposition and solving linear systems for reconstruction.

### [Wavelet Slice Compression (Video Coding Approach)](5379-wavelet-slice-compression-video-coding-approach.md)
Partitions a 3D volume into 2D slices and treats them as a sequence of correlated frames, applying video coding techniques to exploit temporal and spatial coherence. This approach separates spatial compression within slices from [temporal compression](#6719-vector-quantization-for-time-varying-fields.md) between them, leveraging established video compression principles to achieve higher compression ratios for volumetric data with strong inter-slice correlation. Choose this when the volume exhibits strong slice-to-slice redundancy (e.g., MRI stacks).

### [Biorthogonal Wavelet Compression](5381-biorthogonal-wavelet-compression.md)
Compresses volumetric data by applying a multilevel [wavelet transform](#2285-wavelet-transform.md) and discarding the least significant coefficients to achieve variable compression ratios while preserving reconstruction quality. It partitions the volume into blocks and transforms them independently using biorthogonal filters, such as the 9/7-tap [Daubechies wavelet](#5381-biorthogonal-wavelet-compression.md) or biorthogonal spline wavelets. Unlike tensor approximation methods which follow a multiscale behavior, this method exhibits multiresolution behavior, making it advantageous for reconstructing the overall statistical distribution of a dataset at coarser resolutions.

### [Wavelet Compression (Haar Basis)](5779-wavelet-compression-haar-basis.md)
Represents volume data using a smaller set of coefficients derived from the Haar wavelet basis. It solves the problem of reducing memory footprint and bandwidth for volume rendering by exploiting the sparsity of wavelet coefficients, where most energy is concentrated in a few large coefficients. Unlike sibling methods that may use biorthogonal filters or packet transforms, this method relies on the orthogonal Haar basis, allowing for a globally optimal compression strategy via coefficient thresholding (the "Global Oracle") that minimizes the $L^2$ approximation error for a given number of retained coefficients.

### [Discrete Wavelet Packet Transform](6049-discrete-wavelet-packet-transform.md)
Provides a richer, more flexible decomposition of volume data than the standard Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) by recursively decomposing both approximation and detail coefficients. Unlike standard DWT, which only decomposes the low-frequency approximation subband, DWPT allows for arbitrary tree structures, enabling optimal basis selection for specific data characteristics. It is primarily used in [volume segmentation](#12558-reconstruction-and-segmentation.md) rather than volume rendering.

### [3D Discrete Wavelet Transform](6083-3d-discrete-wavelet-transform.md)
Extends the 2D algorithm to volumetric data by applying a separable three-pass filter bank along the $x$, $y$, and $z$ axes. It generates a hierarchical pyramid representation of the volume, serving as the foundational transform for subsequent compression and [rendering stages](#1318-volume-rendering-pipeline.md). Unlike its siblings, it applies a fixed, axis-aligned decomposition hierarchy without adaptive direction selection or integer-only constraints [G].

### [Block-based intra-band prediction](7449-block-based-intra-band-prediction.md)
A lossless compression technique applied to wavelet coefficients to exploit remaining anatomical symmetries and spatial correlations that persist after multi-level decomposition. It operates by predicting a current block of coefficients from previously encoded blocks using geometric transformations (rotations and mirroring), encoding the residual only if it yields a lower bit-rate than encoding the original block. Unlike generic volumetric compression methods, this method is highly specialized for medical images with strong structural symmetries (particularly CT scans) and is ineffective on smooth or non-symmetrical data like MRI or Ultrasound.

### [Lifting-Based Temporal Wavelet Transform](8249-lifting-based-temporal-wavelet-transform.md)
Computes 1-D temporal wavelet transforms on long image sequences without buffering all slices, thereby avoiding artificial Group of Pictures (GOP) boundaries and the severe quality degradations associated with lossy decoding at those boundaries. It sets itself apart from standard block-based temporal transforms by using a finite buffer to continuously process the sequence, creating the effect of infinite memory through an overlap-save-like mechanism.

### [Independent vectors in every channel](8628-independent-vectors-in-every-channel.md)
A multiresolution compression scheme that extracts $k$-dimensional vectors independently within each channel of the wavelet decomposition hierarchy, without correlating data across different resolution levels. It solves the problem of compressing medical volume data by exploiting spatial redundancy within individual frequency bands while maintaining true multiresolution browsing capabilities, distinguishing it from cross-scale methods that sacrifice resolution adaptability for higher compression ratios.

### [Mask Compression Pipeline](9683-mask-compression-pipeline.md)
A multi-stage encoding strategy designed to minimize the storage footprint of binarized learnable masks used in neural field representations (such as TensoRF and TriPlane). It solves the problem of high memory consumption caused by storing sparse binary masks by exploiting the statistical properties of these masks (high sparsity, block-wise structure) through 8-bit casting, Run-Length Encoding (RLE), and Huffman coding. It distinguishes itself from general volume compression methods by operating specifically on the *mask* data structure rather than the volumetric coefficients themselves, and by utilizing level-wise separation to handle the varying sparsity patterns across different Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) decomposition levels.

### [Shearlet Transform](10813-shearlet-transform.md)
Decomposes a volume into directional, anisotropic coefficients that capture geometric features more efficiently than isotropic wavelets, particularly for surfaces with edges. It differs from its siblings by using shear parameters to orient basis functions, providing sparse representations for objects with curved singularities, whereas wavelets and Laplacian pyramids rely on separable or fixed directional filters.

### [Dual-Tree Complex Wavelet Transform](12543-dual-tree-complex-wavelet-transform.md)
A complex wavelet transform that employs two real discrete wavelet transforms (DWTs) to compute the real and imaginary parts of the transform.

#### Modified Dyadic Wavelet with Rice Coding
- [S1] A method using a modified 3-D dyadic wavelet transform tailored to volumetric medical images and an optimized Rice code of very low complexity for scalable lossless coding.

#### 3D Orthogonal Wavelet Approximation
- [S2, unofficial] A three dimensional wavelet approximation for volume data sets presented by Shigeru Muraki [12].
- [S2, unofficial] Build a 3D orthogonal wavelet basis by using all possible tensor products of one dimensional basis function.
- [S2, unofficial] Apply wavelet transforms to volume data to compute wavelet coefficients.
- [S2, unofficial] Remove insignificant coefficients and only use the remaining coefficients.
- [S2, unofficial] Reconstruct an approximation of the original data from the remaining coefficients.

#### Volumetric Decomposition Structure
- [S3] A labeling notation (x,y,z) representing the number of 1D-DWT decompositions along Horizontal (H), Vertical (V), and Axial (A) dimensions, using the Mallat decomposition structure.
- [S3] Recommended in-slice (XY) decomposition levels: Generally, four levels suffice to efficiently compress images in lossless scenarios.
- [S3] Recommended axial (Z) decomposition levels: Near-optimal efficiency for lossless 5x3 is reached at two levels; for some images, a single decomposition suffices. The bit-rate difference between two levels and the best case is below 0.01 bpp.
- [S3] Performing more decomposition levels than necessary increases processor/memory load and reduces random-access efficiency due to larger support widths.
- [S3] Lossless bit-rate increase relative to (6,6,0) decomposition: Varies by image and number of in-slice decompositions using 5x3 kernel.
- [S3] Lossless bit-rate increase relative to (4,4,4) decomposition: Varies by image and number of axial decompositions using 5x3 kernel.

## Background
The use of [wavelets for volume rendering](#1052-wavelet-based-volume-rendering.md) compression emerged in the early 2000s as a means to handle large medical datasets on GPUs. Wetekam et al. [WSKW05] proposed a multiresolution approach using an octree to store wavelet transforms, decoded via FPGA hardware [S1]. Wu et al. [WQ05] introduced a modified 3-D dyadic wavelet transform with Rice coding for medical images [S1]. Laplacian pyramids were adapted for volume rendering by Guthe et al. [GY95], using low-pass filtering and [delta encoding](#1096-delta-encoding.md) to allow on-the-fly reconstruction [S1]. Muraki [12] presented a 3D orthogonal wavelet approximation using tensor products of 1D bases [S2, unofficial]. Guthe et al. [7] demonstrated [hierarchical wavelet representations](#6108-hierarchical-wavelet-compression.md) allowing 30:1 compression without noticeable artifacts [S2, unofficial]. More recent work includes Shearlets for directional features [S1] and [Mask Compression Pipelines](#9683-mask-compression-pipeline.md) for neural field representations [S1][S2, unofficial].
